editorial:
Ever feel like you survived a war just by getting through middle school gym class? You will totally relate to that feeling while watching this quirky little documentary. Instead of a scripted plot, you get to hang out with the actors and crew from the movie Mr. Woodcock as they swap stories about their own gym class nightmares. It feels like sitting around a campfire with friends, listening to everyone complain about dodgeball mishaps and awkward locker room moments. The vibe is light, funny, and very relatable because almost everyone has a story about a gym teacher who took things way too seriously.

What really makes this work is how genuine the stories feel. Since it is a bonus feature, the pacing is quick and it does not overstay its welcome. You get to see a more human side of the stars, which is a huge plus. If you are into lighthearted comedy or just love reminiscing about school, you should definitely check this out. Since it was made for a DVD, you can find it by adding the physical Blu-ray to your home collection or looking for the movie on digital rental platforms like Apple TV. It is a great little palate cleanser between bigger movies.
endingExplained: The documentary wraps up by bringing all the funny and embarrassing stories together to show that these bad memories actually bond people. There is no big plot twist since it is a real-life interview reel, but it ends on a heartwarming note. The cast realizes that their shared trauma from gym class is what makes them laugh today. It finishes with a final montage of smiles and laughs, leaving you feeling glad you are finally out of gym class.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves funny real-life stories about school.
